# **1\. Overview** {#1.-overview}

This design document presents a comprehensive architecture for **Ask AI**, a chatbot solution developed to enhance the Couchbase documentation experience. Ask AI aims to provide users with accurate, contextual answers to their Couchbase-related questions.

# **2\. Problem** {#2.-problem}

To improve the user experience on Capella, providing access to accurate and relevant information is crucial. While we do offer extensive documentation, users often struggle to find precise answers quickly. To address this, we aim to develop a chatbot capable of answering questions related to Couchbase by leveraging the documentation. This solution will act as a technical companion, delivering the right information to users exactly when they need it.

# **3\. Functional Requirements [\[PRD\]](https://docs.google.com/document/d/12jTnPQuO4iMA9PIn9My6dqM_tmTT4cxKuZhcHrfxwhw/edit?tab=t.0)** {#3.-functional-requirements-[prd]}

3.1 Integration

1. Use Couchbase's existing documentation database. \[P0\]  
   1. Phase 1 only supports publicly available documentation.  
   2. Phase 2 will support private preview documentation.  
      *(Use Private LLMs and Embedding models for Private Preview Documents, leverage AI-gateway)*

3.2 User Interaction

1. Natural language processing for conversational experience. \[P0\]  
2. Have an option to provide feedback (Thumbs up / down). \[P0\]  
3. Allow users to provide a comment on the feedback. \[P2\]

3.3 Chat and Navigation

1. Provide links to the actual documentation pages which the user can refer to. \[P0\]  
2. The LLM should be context aware while generating answers. \[P0\]  
3. Maintain chat history. \[P1\]

3.4 Real-Time Assistance

1. Code snippet suggestions \[P0\]  
2. Troubleshooting steps \[P0\]

3.5 Technical Requirements

1. Handle updates in documentation data. \[P0\]  
2. Authentication and Authorization \[P0\]  
3. Have backup for old vector embeddings. And validate the newly created embeddings. \[P1\]  
4. Compliant with data privacy regulations like GDPR. \[P1\]  
5. Rate Limiting. \[P1\]  
6. Support Guardrails, hallucination detection, monitoring \[P1\]

## 4.3 Data Storage {#4.3-data-storage}

### 4.3.1 S3 Bucket

The public documentation is accessed via a replication from an S3 bucket (Staged) used by the documentation site to an S3 bucket named docsbot-data. This bucket is created under aws account having alias dbaas-test-5 and in the US East (Ohio) us-east-2 region. It is used to create embeddings on a weekly basis by the cron job. Following are the number of objects and size (only single version) of this bucket (*as of 28/March/2025).*

![][image3]

The bucket contains html pages for all the topics (latest version only) available on couchbase public documentation site.  
![][image4]

The source links (to public documentation site pages) for these files are generated using the prefix hierarchy of HTML objects in this S3 bucket.

```
Example:
To get the public link for an object with the following S3 URI:
s3://docsbot-data/cloud/clouds/vpc-peering/peer-gcp.html
Replace the prefix s3://docsbot-data to https://docs.couchbase.com.
Link to public doc:
https://docs.couchbase.com/cloud/clouds/vpc-peering/peer-gcp.html
```

### 4.3.2 Vector Store {#4.3.2-vector-store}

The embeddings generated from docsbot-data S3 bucket are stored inside an operational cluster named Docsbot on Capella. Currently this cluster exists on prod under a capella-prod tenant. Following is the hierarchy of the vector database:

```
Bucket: docsbot-<env>
Scope: vector
Collections: 	embeddings 	(extracted text and vector embeddings)
		pages		(text extracted from html docs of S3 bucket)
```

The vector embeddings and the corresponding text are stored under the collection named embeddings. Following is the schema used for documents under this collection:

```
Schema:
{
  _type string  capellaSpecific string  chatbotStageDocsUrl string  chunkIndex number  embedding [number]  id string  pageRef string  pageTitle string  publicDocsUrl string  text string  tokenCount number
}
```

The text extracted from the html docs of S3 bucket are stored under the collection named pages. This collection is used for debugging purposes and does not contribute as a dependency for the functionality of Ask AI. Following is the schema used for documents under this collection:

```
Schema:
{
  _type string  chatbotStageDocsUrl string  chunksCreated number  content string  id string  publicDocsUrl string
}
```

### 4.3.3 Feedback Store

User feedback for Ask AI interactions is maintained in a dedicated operational cluster called Docsbot on Capella. (same as [Vector Store](#4.3.2-vector-store)). Currently this cluster exists on prod under capella-prod tenant. 

**What are these feedbacks?**

Feedback in this context refers to user evaluations of Ask AI's responses. When users interact with Ask AI by submitting queries, they have the opportunity to rate the quality and relevance of the responses they receive. This rating system is binary:

* Thumbs Up: Indicates a positive user experience, suggesting the response was helpful and relevant  
* Thumbs Down: Indicates a negative user experience, suggesting the response did not adequately address the user's query 

Following is the hierarchy of the feedback store:

```
Bucket: docsbot-<env>
Scope: _default
Collections: _default
```

The feedback along with the user query and respective response is stored under the collection named feedbacks. Following is the schema used for documents under this collection:

```
Schema:
{
	_type string
comment string
feedbackType string
id string
query string
queryId string
response string
submittedAt string
tags array | null
tenantId string
}
```

## 4.4 Component Level Design {#4.4-component-level-design}

Couchbase Capella: (Link: [Ask AI Sequence Diagram Couchbase Capella](https://app.diagrams.net/?title=DocsBot_Sequence_Diagram_Couchbase_Capella.drawio&client=1#G11soRCpmF4xdWNUpnrbynnD0GfVtlDwp5#%7B%22pageId%22%3A%22NJm0z59eM27ffH1g1ab7%22%7D))

![][image5]

### 4.4.1 CP-UI

For Capella UI, the user interface for Ask AI is integrated into the CP-UI. The current setup includes a button located in the navbar, ensuring Ask AI is accessible from any page, as the navbar is consistently present across most Capella pages. Clicking this button opens a pop-over where users can submit their queries \[[Figma Design](https://www.figma.com/design/ZFqvp5IjnUCHA351gV9Z2p/Chatbot?node-id=619-28485&m=dev)\].

When a user submits a query, it is sent to the CP-API along with a **JWT token** obtained during login. The request also includes the user's **Tenant ID** as a parameter. The payload of the request comprises the user's query, queryId and the chat history.

**Chat History and Context (localStorage)**

Ask AI UI uses the browser's localStorage to persist chat history locally on the client side. When a user submits a new query, the UI retrieves the last five interactions from the stored history and includes them as part of the request payload to the backend. This allows the chatbot to maintain conversational context and provide more relevant, coherent answers.

### 4.4.3 CP-API

The CP-API serves as the intermediary between the CP-UI and the Ask AI backend, managing requests and responses for the Ask AI streaming functionality.

**Key Responsibilities of CP-API:**

1. **JWT Token Verification**  
   The CP- API ensures that each incoming request contains a valid **JWT token**, providing a layer of security and authentication.

2. **Request Handling**  
   The **DocsBotStream** handler is responsible for processing incoming requests. It validates the tenantID from the request parameters and determines whether the tenant is on a free or paid plan. This distinction is crucial as the [iQ Backend](#4.4.6-iq-backend) enforces different [rate limits](#4.4.9-rate-limits) based on whether the tenant is paid or free.

3. **Payload Validation**  
   Before processing, the API verifies the integrity and structure of the payload received from the client.

4. **Streaming Response**  
   Utilizing the Ask AI backend logic, the API streams responses back to the user. This involves generating a response using the **Ask AI service** and handling the streaming of this response to the client.

5. **Metrics Tracking**  
   The API tracks various metrics, such as the number of input and output tokens used for each AI model call and the time taken to complete the request. This data is essential for monitoring performance and for [cost analysis](#6.-cost-analysis).  
   

This design ensures that the CP-API efficiently manages requests, maintains security, and provides a seamless streaming experience for users interacting with the Ask AI service.

### 4.4.5 Hybrid Search with Re-ranking

Ask AI uses a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) approach to provide contextually accurate responses by retrieving relevant documentation content based on user queries. The system has evolved from pure vector search to a sophisticated hybrid search approach that combines both vector similarity and full-text search capabilities for improved retrieval accuracy.

**Query Processing Flow**

1. **User Query Embedding**  
   When a request submits a query, the iQ Backend converts this query into a rephrased query (based on the previous chat history) via an LLM call to openAI. This rephrased query is then converted into a vector embedding using iQ backend.

2. **Hybrid Search**  
   The system performs a hybrid search that combines two complementary search methods:  
   * *Vector Search Component*: Uses the generated query embedding to perform vector similarity search against the pre-indexed vector space  
   * *Full-Text Search Component*: Performs traditional text-based search using the rephrased query against the document text content

This hybrid approach leverages Couchbase's native hybrid search capabilities, executing both search methods simultaneously in a single query operation. The search is conducted using the Couchbase Go SDK against the configured search index.

3. **Fallback Mechanism**  
   If the hybrid search returns no results, the system automatically falls back to pure vector search to ensure query coverage.

4. **Custom Re-ranking**  
   After retrieving the initial results from hybrid search, the system applies a custom re-ranking algorithm that:  
   * Combines the base search scores with additional custom scoring factors  
   * Applies length-based scoring preferences (favoring medium-length chunks)  
   * Provides content-type bonuses for code examples, headings, and structured content

5. **Result Enrichment**  
   Each retrieved and re-ranked result includes:  
   * The content matched for that particular embedding and text query  
   * The original URL pointing to the relevant page on the public documentation site  
   * Enhanced scoring information from both vector similarity and text relevance  
   * Metadata including page title, chunk index, and token count

6. **Context for LLM**  
   The top K re-ranked documents (currently K \= 5\) are combined with the rephrased user query to form the prompt context for the LLM. This hybrid approach with custom re-ranking provides the model with accurate and diverse grounding information, enabling it to generate better-informed responses.

**Search Logging and Analytics**

The system maintains comprehensive search logs that track:

* Search type used (hybrid vs. vector fallback)  
* Initial search results before re-ranking  
* Re-ranked results after custom scoring  
* Final results sent to the LLM  
* Performance metrics and score statistics

### 4.4.6 iQ Backend {#4.4.6-iq-backend}

The iQ Backend serves as an abstraction layer over the OpenAI APIs, offering controlled and streamlined access to core LLM capabilities used by Ask AI.

**Functionality**

Ask AI leverages the iQ Backend for two primary operations:

1. CreateEmbeddings

   * Converts user queries into vector embeddings, which are then used for performing similarity search against the documentation embedded in vector store.  
   * Requires Tenant ID \+ User ID

2. CreateChatCompletionsStream

   * Generates streamed LLM responses based on the user’s query combined with the retrieved context documents.  
   * Requires Tenant ID \+ User ID

**Rate Limiting and Usage Control**

The iQ Backend also introduces rate-limiting mechanisms to regulate usage of the underlying OpenAI services. It provides:

* Checks based on tenant identity (Valid and Free or Paid)  
* Limits on calls per minute  
* Limits on requests per day  
* Limits on tokens per month

These controls ensure stable and fair access to LLM resources across multiple deployments while preventing abuse or runaway costs.

### 4.4.7 CP-Jobs

To ensure Ask AI has access to the most up-to-date information, the knowledge base must reflect the latest updates from the documentation site, which is frequently revised.

**Automated Embedding Pipeline**

To automate this process, a cron job is set up within CP-Jobs and scheduled to run weekly using CP-Scheduler. The job executes the following steps:

1. Fetch Latest Documentation  
   Retrieves all HTML files (objects) from the specified S3 bucket that contains the public documentation.

2. Cleanup  
   Extracts only the relevant content from each HTML object, omitting headers, footers, and sidebars.

3. Chunking  
   Breaks down each HTML page into smaller chunks to ensure the accuracy of the resulting vector embeddings.

4. Generate New Embeddings  
   Processes each chunk through the OpenAI’s text-embedding-3-small model to create updated vector embeddings.

5. Store Embeddings  
   Saves the newly generated embeddings to the vector store, either replacing or versioning over the previous embeddings.

This pipeline ensures that Ask AI continuously reflects the most current state of the documentation, providing users with accurate and relevant answers.

**Sandbox Testing and Resource Usage**  
The cron job was tested out on a sandbox, and the resource usage by CP-Jobs can be found [here](https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/qx2-mkj-mk3/cp-jobs?fromUser=false&refresh_mode=paused&tpl_var_cluster%5B0%5D=sbx-10-cp-eks&tpl_var_environment%5B0%5D=sandbox&tpl_var_trace_environment%5B0%5D=sandbox&from_ts=1749744300000&to_ts=1749745500000&live=false).  
The job takes around **5-6 hours** to complete when it is **synchronous**. We added goroutines to make it faster, which reduced the time to 20 minutes.  
Currently, we have **10 routines**; if we let it run for more time, we could reduce the number of routines. That would bring down the CPU usage if there's a concern.

### 4.4.8 Context Aware LLM {#4.4.8-context-aware-llm}

Before performing vector search, the user query—along with recent chat history—is passed to a lightweight LLM for context-aware rephrasing.

The goal is to convert the query into a fully self-contained and explicit form, resolving any vague references (e.g., “this”, “it”, “these”) based on prior conversation. This ensures the rephrased query accurately reflects the user's intent without relying on implicit context.

By doing this:

* We significantly improve the relevance of documents retrieved via vector search.  
* We can optionally correct spelling or minor language issues before retrieval.  
* We avoid using a second large LLM call, thus keeping cost and latency low.

Only the rephrased query and the top retrieved documents are sent to the main LLM for response generation. This design maintains context awareness, enhances retrieval precision, and optimizes for performance and cost efficiency.

### 4.4.9 Rate Limits {#4.4.9-rate-limits}

Rate limiting helps protect a system by controlling how often users can make API requests. It prevents overloading the system and ensures fair access for everyone. By limiting request frequency, the system stays reliable and performs well, preventing denial-of-service attacks and resource abuse. This way, legitimate users can continue using the service without interruptions, even during high-traffic periods.

The following components have been rate limited:

**iQ Backend:**

IQ enforces rate limits to ensure equitable resource distribution. The limits applied are as follows:

Calls Limit: This limit is based on the number of API calls made per minute (with a configurable time range between 1 minute and 1 hour) per tenant, targeting the endpoint. This helps mitigate Denial of Service (DoS) attacks.(“Calls limit exceeded” error response if violates)

Requests Limit: This limit governs the number of requests that can be sent by a user (at the individual user level) within a specified period of time. E.g.: 2000 calls per day (“Requests limit exceeded" error if violates)

Token Limit: This limit tracks the number of tokens consumed versus the total number allowed for each tenant. E.g. 2 million tokens per month (a “Tokens limit exceeded” error response if violates)

The specific limits for iQ are:

```
IQ_INTEGRATION_CALLS_RATE_LIMIT_ALLOWED=100
IQ_INTEGRATION_CALLS_RATE_LIMIT_PERIOD_SECS=60
IQ_INTEGRATION_REQUESTS_RATE_LIMIT_ALLOWED=2000
IQ_INTEGRATION_REQUESTS_RATE_LIMIT_PERIOD_SECS=86400
IQ_INTEGRATION_TOKENS_RATE_LIMIT_ALLOWED=500000
IQ_INTEGRATION_TOKENS_RATE_LIMIT_PERIOD_SECS=2592000
IQ_INTEGRATION_PAID_REQUESTS_RATE_LIMIT_ALLOWED=2000
IQ_INTEGRATION_PAID_REQUESTS_RATE_LIMIT_PERIOD_SECS=86400
IQ_INTEGRATION_PAID_TOKENS_RATE_LIMIT_ALLOWED=2000000
IQ_INTEGRATION_PAID_TOKENS_RATE_LIMIT_PERIOD_SECS=2592000
```

# 

# **5\. Dependencies** {#5.-dependencies}

The below are some of known dependencies for the Ask AI:

5.1 AWS S3 Bucket

Serves as the primary data source for Ask AI. All documentation content is stored here before being processed into embeddings, making it the foundation of our knowledge base architecture. Maintained by [\#documentation](https://couchbase.slack.com/archives/CC7UY6MM4) team.

5.2 OpenAI Models

* GPT-4o: Used for rephrasing query and making it independent of context history. And, Powers response generation, enabling the chatbot to provide coherent, contextually relevant answers.  
* text-embedding-3-small: Creates vector embeddings from documentation content, facilitating efficient semantic search capabilities.

5.3 Vector Database

Critical infrastructure component that enables similarity search functionality. This database stores and indexes all document embeddings, directly impacting response quality by determining what contextual information is retrieved and included with each user prompt. System availability depends heavily on this component's operational status.

Vector Database Deployment:

* Implement a separate, purpose-built database with the latest vector search functionality.  
* Specifications:  
  1. Single Node (version 7.6 and above) preferably 7.6.4+ as it supports most of the features required for FTS along with cosine similarity metrics.  
  2. Services required by the cluster:  
     1. Data Service 		\- To Store text and vector embeddings  
     2. Query Service 	\- Used by feedback loop logic  
     3. Search Service	\- To perform vector search  
     4. Index Service		\- To index and query data when we add support for monitoring

# **7\. Concerns / Risks** {#7.-concerns-/-risks}

This section outlines potential failure scenarios for Docbot, their impacts, and mitigation strategies.

1. **Irrelevant Document Retrieval**  
* *Scenario: A user asks for information about "Operational Cluster," but the chatbot retrieves documents related to "Columnar Cluster," leading to confusion and inaccurate responses.*   
* Impact: Inaccurate or hallucinated responses.  
* Mitigation: Implement semantic filtering and hybrid retrieval combining keyword and vector search.  
2. **Missing Documentation**  
* *Scenario: A user inquires about a Couchbase server 7.2, but the chatbot responds with "I don't know" because the relevant documentation is missing from the vector store.*  
* Impact: Incomplete or "I don't know" responses  
* Mitigation: Clearly communicate the scope and limitations of available documentation to users.  
3. **Vector Database Downtime**  
* *Scenario: During a peak usage period, the Couchbase vector search service goes down, resulting in the chatbot being unable to retrieve any documents, leading to complete retrieval failure.*  
* Impact: Complete retrieval failure  
* Mitigation: Deploy health monitoring with automated alerts, read replicas for fault tolerance, and circuit breaker patterns. Serve cached responses for common queries during outages to maintain basic functionality.  
4. **LLM API Failures**  
* *Scenario: OpenAI's service experiences a disruption or rate limiting, causing the Ask AI to be unable to generate responses, resulting in failure to answer any user query.*  
* Impact: Generation service unavailable. Ask AI will fail to answer any query.  
* Mitigation: Implement retry mechanisms and multiple LLM provider fallbacks. Cache responses for common queries to reduce API dependency during outages.  
5. **OpenAI Embedding Service Disruption**  
* *Scenario: During a scheduled documentation update, OpenAI's embedding API becomes unavailable, preventing new or updated documentation from being vectorized and added to the search index.*  
* Impact: Ask AI will continue using old vector embeddings.  
* Mitigation: Implement automated resumable cron jobs in case of failures with retries. Alternative embedding models can be used in case of longer disruptions.  
6. **Insufficient Storage**  
* *Scenario: In case of release of a new product like AI-Services, private preview documentation would be moved to public access, the increased data volume may exceed the current vector database's capacity, requiring expansion.*  
* Impact: Incomplete embeddings, affecting response accuracy for new product documentation.  
* Mitigation: Can use Storage Auto-Expansion provided by Capella.  
7. **Ethical & Legal Risks**  
* *Scenario: A user interacts with the chatbot to seek medical advice, and the chatbot provides incorrect or misleading information that leads to harm.*  
* Impact: Legal issues and reputational damage.  
* Mitigation: Implement usage policies, implement guardrails and provide disclaimers.

# **8\. Troubleshooting** {#8.-troubleshooting}

This section outlines troubleshooting steps to determine why the Ask AI might be unable to answer a question. If a user receives the response, "I'm sorry, I don't have enough information to answer that," there could be several reasons for this. By following these steps, you can identify the underlying cause.

1. Verify the Question's Relevance   
     
   Ensure the question is appropriate for Ask AI. For example, if the question is *"What is React?"*, the response *"I'm sorry, I don't have enough information to answer that."* is expected, as the Ask AI is designed to address only Couchbase-related inquiries.  
     
2. Examine the Context

   Check if the vector search returns any context. If no context is returned, there may be an issue with the vector store. If context is returned but unrelated to the query, proceed to the next steps.

3. Review the Public Documentation

   The question might pertain to Couchbase, but relevant documentation may be missing. Ensure the documentation contains the necessary information. For instance, if a user asks, "How to turn off my cluster" and receives no answer, verify that the relevant page, such as [this one](https://docs.couchbase.com/cloud/clusters/off-on-database.html), is available and contains the required details.

4. Check the Chatbot Staging Documentation

   Copy the relative path from the public docs URL and append it to [https://chatbot-staging.docs-test.couchbase.com/](https://chatbot-staging.docs-test.couchbase.com/). Verify if the page exists and contains the same information. This is crucial because this site reflects the data stored in the S3 bucket mentioned [here](#4.3-data-storage). If no data is found, it indicates that the S3 bucket is missing the necessary data.

5. Inspect the Pages Collection in the Vector Store  
     
   If the data is present in the S3 bucket, the next step is to examine the vector store. Log in to the Capella instance where the vector store is located (currently in [sbx-11](https://ui.sbx-11.sandbox.nonprod-project-avengers.com/)) and navigate to the pages collection. Search for the public docs URL (each document uses the public docs URL as its ID). If the document is missing, there was likely an issue extracting the HTML content from the S3 bucket. If the document is present, ensure it contains the required data.   
     
6. Examine the Embedding Collection in the Vector Store  
     
   If relevant data is found in the pages collection, the embedding collection should contain the chunks created from this page along with their embeddings. If chunks are missing, there was likely an issue during the embedding creation process.  
     
7. Match the Returned Chunks to the Expected Chunks  
     
   The chunks created from the page should be returned by the vector search. If different, unrelated chunks are returned, there may be a problem with the vector search or the accuracy of the created embeddings.

# **9\. Non Functional Requirements** {#9.-non-functional-requirements}

9.1 Scalability

The system must efficiently handle varying loads with the ability to scale horizontally as demand increases. The vector database and retrieval system should accommodate the full Couchbase documentation corpus while maintaining consistent retrieval times regardless of database size. Auto-scaling capabilities will manage traffic spikes, particularly during product releases or events, ensuring consistent performance under all conditions.

9.2 Latency and Availability

Ask AI must provide responsive interactions with minimal waiting times for users, employing streaming responses to enhance perceived performance. The system should maintain high availability during business hours across global time zones. Maintenance activities must be scheduled with minimal user impact, and the architecture should eliminate single points of failure through redundancy and fallback mechanisms.

9.3 Maintainability

To support maintainability and ease of debugging, Ask AI includes a robust logging mechanism across all major components. This logging tracks key events, API calls, and error traces throughout the system from the UI and the backend services.

9.4 Security  
The system will implement rate limiting to prevent abuse and input validation to guard against injection attacks. Authentication will integrate with existing Couchbase Cloud systems, and all LLM interactions will be filtered to prevent prompt injection vulnerabilities. Regular security audits and compliance with data privacy regulations will be maintained throughout the system lifecycle.

# **10\. Testing** {#10.-testing}

Currently we test Ask AI in [this](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ji6j3WoIP3d1F4z3SHUQ-u6pT7MsBOBqsKCjfKY-_VI/edit?usp=sharing) google sheet. In the sheet we provide the prompt and the expected answer from Ask AI. We have a [python script](https://github.com/couchbasecloud/docsbot-backend/blob/main/docsbot-testing/update_sheet.py) which ( manually triggered ) runs to generate the response ( from Ask AI ) and then compares it with the expected answer.  
It generates the following metrics:

1. Similarity Score  
* Cosine similarity between vector embeddings from OpenAI's text-embedding-ada-002 model.  
* Scale: 0.0 to 1.0 (higher indicates greater semantic similarity).  
* Provides a quantitative, model-based measurement of how closely the semantic content matches.  
2. Insights  
* Generated by OpenAI's GPT-4 model through prompt engineering.  
* Concise qualitative assessment of response quality, highlighting strengths, weaknesses, and differences.  
* Offers human-readable explanation beyond numerical similarity, focusing on contextual relevance and correctness.  
3. Classification Label  
* Categorical classification by GPT-4 into one of four predefined categories  
  * Matched: The generated response closely aligns with the expected answer.  
  * Improves upon: The generated response contains the expected information plus valuable additions.  
  * Partially correct: The generated response contains some but not all expected information.  
  * Completely different: The generated response significantly deviates from expectations.

# **11\. Future Improvements** {#11.-future-improvements}

* Improve prompt and response logging with detailed insights.  
* Add semantic caching to allow quick responses to frequently asked questions. (We could leverage caching provided by AI-gateway).  
* Use IndexDB instead of localStorage to store chat history, as localStorage offers a maximum of 5MB per website domain.  
* Depending on the page where the user is currently the bot can suggest some questions or give them most frequently asked questions for that page or topic.  
* When inside Capella, the bot can include links to relevant Capella pages / sections while giving users certain action steps to enhance user experience.  
* The bot can be designed to recognize the content of the page and automatically include relevant data in its responses. *For instance, if a user is viewing a specific Capella cluster, the bot could use that context to automatically insert the correct connection string into a generated SDK code.*  
  * Integrate with AI Assistant

# **12\. Open Questions** {#12.-open-questions}

**1\. S3 Bucket Location**

We have the S3 bucket created in AWS dbaas-test-5 account. When we move to production:

1. What would be the location of the S3 bucket? Are we going to use the one in the dev account (dbaas-test-5) only?  
2. If we maintain separate S3 buckets, then would we be having S3 buckets for both prod as well as stage environments?  
3. Need to consider the replication that will be set on these buckets. Currently we have the following replication:  
   (Docs team staged S3 bucket)      —-------\>     (dbaas-test-5 dev account S3 bucket)

**2\. Versioning of S3 Bucket Replicated Objects**

The daily batch replication job from the Docs team’s S3 bucket is creating new versions daily for all objects, leading to **linear growth** in the bucket's size. Over time, this will significantly increase storage costs. To manage this, we need to decide how many versions of each object should be retained.

A possible workaround could be:

1. Writing a Lambda function that:  
   1. Lists all versions of each object.  
   2. Retains the latest **n** versions based on the timestamp.  
   3. Deletes older versions.  
2. This function can be scheduled with EventBridge as a daily or weekly job to automate the process.
